title: Negative: a mature r-two56 cog has no fission state within single-kernel changes of +-5-25%: 40/48 stay one non-growing cog, 7 die, 1 becomes a self-annihilating expanding ring
summary: The question's last arm asks whether weakening r-two56's size limiter lets cogs divide. I planted one food-fed cog of the lcn-cog world in a 96^2 box and perturbed each of its 6 kernels in turn (m +-5% and +-10%, h +-25%, s +-15%; 48 runs of 400 t). None divided: 40 stayed one cog of constant mass, 7 died, and one (k1 m x0.9) grew as a closed ring that annihilated itself across the box. Together with the lcn worm results (k0 x0.6-0.7 gives unbounded worms, not cells), this closes the single-parameter route to cog fission.

finding.operator: single-kernel perturbation of the r-two56 rule (size limiter and others)
finding.control: unperturbed cog in the same box (1 cog, matter 1.00 at t=400)
finding.result: 0/48 fission; 40 stable single cogs (matter 0.95-1.02), 7 deaths, 1 expanding self-annihilating ring
